name: Musroomfolk, Bolite
body:
Physical Description: Bolites tend to be around 3 feet in height, though some specimens reach nearly 4. Their bodies are primarily composed of a pale, spongy fiber that can get surprisingly tough on older bolites. Their legs end in stumpy flares, similar in outline to an elephant’s foot in miniature. Their arms always seem to be proportional, though the number (and size & length) of fingers varies from hand to hand—some sporting as few as three and others as many as eight, though never in an unusable configuration somehow. They lack a discernible neck separating their torsos from their simple, noseless faces. Their caps often have patterns, mostly spots, and are prone to being vibrantly colored. The underside of the caps, the lamella, glow with a soft light of almost any colour of the rainbow. Bolites vary greatly in width, ranging from having nearly the girth of a barrel to looking like a behatted fencepost. Bolites have no gender, although those who spend time around gendered races may find enjoyment in affecting a gendered personality.

Relations: Bolites get along well with all other castes of agarician society. Beyond the fungal folk however, most bolites are woefully uneducated, unable to tell a halfling from a gnome. When in their own territory they will often become reclusive around outsiders, preferring to let more powerful agaricians deal with outside threats. Those who venture into the world beyond are typically cautious about dealing with unknown races, and are often quick to categorize friend from foe based on first encounters.

Alignment & Religion: Bolites believe that their existence is cyclical in nature, and they look to natural cycles of decay and rebirth for their spirituality rather than gods. This casts a shadow on any bolites who choose to wander however, as each knows that they must return to their bloom for the cycle to continue. If a bolite knows that it will die before it can return to its bloom, it will try to arrange for its remains to be delivered. Such a task is not something requested lightly, nor is it a service soon forgotten by the bloom.

Adventurers: The most common reason for a bolite to leave the bloom is to serve as the eyes for a sibyl, and few eyes roam farther than those of an adventurer. The bolites themselves find the dynamic of an adventuring group to be a natural fit, and prove to be staunch allies once they’re certain their trust isn’t being misplaced. The sibyl the bolite answers to, if any, will usually see the value in having an allied group of adventurers, and may even offer assistance if the bolite can vouch for them.

Names: A bolite’s agarician name is untranslatable, and any who come to interact with non-agaricians quickly learn the value of adopting a pronounceable name. Some take interesting names that they’ve heard as their own, while others invent names for themselves based on nothing more than what sounds are fun to say. A lucky few even take suggestions from hopefully benevolent teammates.

Traits

Bolites are defined by their class levels—they do not possess racial Hit Dice. All bolites have the following racial traits:

Type (10 RP) Bolites are plants with the fungus subtype. Further, they are immune to paralysis, poison, sleep effects, and stunning. Finally bolites breathe and eat, but do not sleep, unless they want to gain some beneficial effect from this activity. This means that a bolites can sleep in order to regain spells, but sleep is not required to survive or stay in good health.
Small (0 RP) Bolites are Small creatures and gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on combat maneuver checks and to their CMD, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.
Speed (0 RP) Bolites have a base speed of 30 feet. +2 Dexterity, +2 Wisdom, -2 Charisma (0 RP) Though quick and insightful, bolites have a hard time relating to most non-fungal creatures, and even the most outgoing among them struggle with communicating without the use of light and chemistry.
Luminous Lamella (Ex) (0 RP) Select a color upon character creation. The underside of a bolite’s cap emits a soft, steady glow in that shade with light equivalent to a candle. Although they can’t suppress this effect, and it persists for some time after death, it is relatively easy to cover with clothing should the need arise. The color a bolite glows varies from individual to individual, and although they can’t consciously change it, it will subtly respond to changes in their health and mood.
Poison (Ex) (2 RP) injury; save Fort DC 10 + 1/2 the user’s Hit Dice + the user’s Constitution modifier; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d2 Str; cure 1 save.
Mutable (Ex) (-2 RP) Bolites are created to be adaptable to whatever role they need to fill within a bloom. Despite being plants, they are not immune to mind-affecting effects or polymorph effects.
Low-Light Vision (0 RP- included in type) Bolites have low-light vision, allowing them to see twice as far as humans in dim light.
